scope: Books 10–16 source-intake decisions; no lesson changes or selection

findings.explanation: “Stumbling around in the dark” means proceeding without enough knowledge or guidance, essentially the same darkness-and-uncertainty learner outcome as canonical 1916 “grope in the dark”. The different motion verb alone is not an explained new sense.
findings.recommendedFix: Hold pending canonical 1916 scope/pattern review or document a genuine pragmatic/construction distinction before assigning a new owner.

findings.explanation: “Progress begins when you keep showing up” means continuing to participate and put in effort, not simply arriving at a meeting. Proposed owner 2123 explicitly teaches literal arrival/appearance and contrasts that with promised attendance; aliasing this motivational persistence use to 2123 would misteach the source meaning.
findings.recommendedFix: Move 4122 to hold-editorial pending a persistence-versus-arrival sense decision, or assign a separate owner with repeated-effort models if justified.

findings.explanation: “Feedback helped her get past it” gives no antecedent for “it” in the source sentence. The proposed lesson claims obstacle-overcoming, but the stand-alone source cannot establish whether it refers to a mistake, feeling, task or physical object.
findings.recommendedFix: Hold or supply a clearly grounded guide-written context/model and record the pronoun ambiguity in the decision before drafting.

findings.explanation: “That photograph left a mental snapshot I could still recall” is semantically redundant: a photograph is already a snapshot, and “mental snapshot I could still recall” repeats the memory idea. The intended idiom is valid but the source is weak as a natural model.
findings.recommendedFix: Retain exact source provenance but require a more natural guide-written mental-snapshot model and mark the source awkwardness in the decision.
